newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate OKs lottery bill to aid schools.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate OKs lottery bill to aid schools.

text.p: California's Senate on Thursday approved a bill that would redirect more than $60 million a year of state lottery revenues to public schools.

The Senate approved the bill by Democratic Senator Steve Peace on a vote of 30-to-0, sending the measure to the Assembly for review. Earlier this week, a similar bill, Senate Bill 249, also cleared the Senate.
Peace's bill, Senate Bill 1193, would reduce the percentage of total state lottery revenues that can be allocated for administrative expenses and redirect those funds to public schools.
Under measure, the percentage of total state lottery revenues that could be allocated for administrative expenses would be reduced from 16 percent to 12 percent.
The shift would provide schools and universities with more than $60 million a year, depending on lottery revenues, state officials said.

Current law calls for 50 percent of lottery revenues to be returned to the public in the form of prizes, 34 percent for public education and no more than 16 percent for payment of expenses of the lottery.
If approved by the Assembly and signed by the governor, the measure would appear on the statewide ballot for voter approval.
